evidence.field: 形義源流通解; 甲骨、金文、說文
evidence.text: The entry reports 后 in late Spring and Autumn bronze inscriptions with the sense ‘ruler’. It says direction distinguishes 后 and 司 in bronze forms but not oracle forms, attributes a same-graph interpretation to Tang Lan and Li Xiaoding, and separately reports Wang Guowei’s identification of an oracle form written with 毓. These are competing accounts; it does not supply a settled component analysis or a graphic sequence into the received form.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫：后

evidence.field: 《說文》; 《廣韻》; 形義源流通解
evidence.text: The page reproduces Shuowen’s definition of 后 as a successor ruler and its account of a human figure issuing commands, analyzed with 一 and 口. It gives Guangyun fanqie 胡口 and 胡遘 in upper and departing tone categories. This records historical lexicographic claims and readings, not proof of the proposed graph analysis.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫：后

evidence.source: Taiwan Ministry of Education Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants
evidence.text: The entry distinguishes 后 and 後 as originally unrelated graphs, reports textual substitution based on their homophony, and gives examples including Yili 大射 and Liji 大學. It says Song–Yuan and later popular literature also used 后 for 後, and that mainland simplified-character tables issued in 1964 and 1986 used 后 as the simplified form of 後. These are the dictionary’s account of the spelling loan and standardization; the cited examples do not establish the earliest loan date.
evidence.title: [A01287-012] 后 (後) - 教育部《異體字字典》

evidence.source: Taiwan Ministry of Education Revised Mandarin Dictionary
evidence.text: The entry gives Mandarin hòu and separately lists ‘king’, ‘feudal lord’, and ‘ruler’s principal wife’, with received-text citations from Shijing 商頌·玄鳥, Zuozhuan 僖公三十二年, Shujing 舜典, and Han shu 景帝紀. It also records 后 for ‘later’ as 通後, citing Liji 大學. These citations document uses but do not date transitions among senses.
evidence.title: 教育部《重編國語辭典修訂本》：后

evidence.field: 後; graphic history and cited bronze/oracle examples
evidence.text: The 後 entry reports an oracle-bone use in 屯南2358 for succession/order, bronze examples for lagging, temporal ‘after’, descendants, and an asserted ‘end’ sense, and Warring States bamboo examples for descendants/successor. Its analysis of early 幺 + 夂 as cord plus foot is explicitly accompanied by an alternative treating 幺 as phonetic. This is a database summary with inscription and manuscript references, not an independent examination of their primary editions.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫：後

search_audit.outcome: Opened both Ministry dictionary pages. The variant dictionary provides its account of classical spelling substitution, examples and 1964/1986 standardization; the revised dictionary gives received-text senses and citations.
The exact file description page, direct image and imageinfo API were attempted; all returned internal errors/cache misses. Candidate provenance remains unverified in this session.
Inspected the exact Commons page, which identifies a modern Lesser Seal drawing and CC BY-SA 3.0 terms. The page’s original-image link was followed, but the direct SVG fetch returned a cache miss.

gaps: No independently inspected primary inscription edition establishes the earliest oracle use of 后; the CUHK page reports late Spring and Autumn bronze attestation for the ruler sense, but does not settle the identity of any earlier oracle forms.

The early graphic account remains disputed: the 后/司 same-graph or orientation account and Wang Guowei’s reported 毓 spelling do not establish a full sequence into received 后. No secure childbirth, rear-body, or component decomposition, nor a corruption path, was established.

Received-text dictionary citations establish ruler, feudal lord, ruler’s-wife, and ‘later/after’ uses, but do not date transitions among the first three senses or prove a childbirth-to-succession semantic chain.

The opened source reports classical spelling substitution of 后 for 後 and later standardized simplification. Exact earliest loan chronology and the ancient sound comparison are unresolved; modern hòu homophony is not ancient phonological evidence.
The packet’s local Unihan and Baxter–Sagart rows were checked as supplied, but Unicode’s character-specific pages and the Baxter–Sagart source PDF were not accessible in this browsing session.
